text: What holds the trunk open? This little strut.
Inside, nitrogen gas is squeezed to a high pressure.
A tiny hole in the piston lets the gas fill both sides.
But on one side, the rod takes up room. So there's less area for the gas to push on.
The push out wins, so the rod always slides out and holds the lid up.
Squeezed gas pushes the rod out. Always.
